extracted.intended_audience: organizations and investigators preparing Full Proposals for the FY25 MURI announcements (ONR / ARO / AFOSR)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting full proposals to the FY25 MURI Funding Opportunity Announcements for ONR, ARO, and AFOSR, including required forms, proposal format, budget preparation, compliance, and registration steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register with SAM / Provide UEI
rubrics_metrics.description: All organizations applying online through FedConnect or Grants.gov must register with the System for Award Management (SAM) and will receive a unique entity identifier (UEI) number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM registration must be renewed annually. Failure to register with SAM will prevent your organization from applying. A Federal awarding agency may not make an award until the Applicant has complied with all UEI and SAM requirements. SAM may be accessed at https://www.sam.gov/SAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect account creation and SAM MPIN
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying through FedConnect, create a FedConnect account. If you are the first person in your organization to register in FedConnect, your SAM Marketing Partner ID (SAM MPIN) will also be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FedConnect registration steps; see FedConnect Ready_Set_Go.pdf for guidance. Do NOT use the FedConnect message center to submit white paper responses or questions related to this announcement; email the point of contact in Section G instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance for FedConnect registration and submission is available from the FedConnect Support Team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email: fcsupport@unisonglobal.com. Phone: 1-800-899-6665. Hours: Monday – Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. EDT. Closed on Federal holidays. Also consult ONR FedConnect FAQs: https://www.nre.navy.mil/work-with-us/how-to-apply/frequently-asked-questions

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit white papers via Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must NOT be submitted through the Grants.gov application process. White paper submissions to ONR must be submitted through FedConnect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific submission channel instructions for white papers vs full proposals. Use FedConnect for white papers to ONR.

rubrics_metrics.name: File attachment format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Files attached to forms must be in Adobe Portable Document Format (.PDF); cannot contain macros; and cannot be password protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any attachment is not a PDF, contains macros, or is password protected, it will not pass automated acceptance checks and must be resubmitted prior to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Proposal formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Proposal must follow specific format: Paper size 8.5 x 11 inch; Margins 1 inch; Spacing single-spaced; Font Times New Roman, 12-point; Page Limit Technical Proposal: 25 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no page limitations for the budget. Be careful about what is included/excluded from the 25-page count (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-count inclusions and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which parts of the submission are included in the Technical Proposal page limit and which are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly noted: Technical Approach / Project Narrative, Management Approach, and Principal Investigator Qualifications are 'included in page count.' Data Management Plan is 'not included in page count.' Cover page and Table of Contents are not included in page count. Confirm placement and length of each section per FOA instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Conflict of Commitment and Conflict of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: All current and pending research support (as defined by Section 223 of the FY21 NDAA) must be disclosed at the time of proposal for all covered individuals; disclosures must be updated annually and whenever covered individuals are added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered individuals = key personnel listed on proposals (e.g., PI, Co-PI). Failure to fully report may be considered a material statement under the False Claims Act. The funding agency may conduct a pre-award conflict review (NSPM-33); significant conflicts may be a basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic file name length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic file name for all documents submitted under this FOA must not exceed 68 characters in length, including the file name extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep filenames concise and within the 68-character limit to avoid submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of SF-424 (R&R) family forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete the mandatory SF-424 Research and Related (R&R) family forms found on Grants.gov and use the SF-424 (R&R) as the cover page for all proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-424 first because some fields auto-populate other forms. Use Grants.gov form guidance: https://www.grants.gov/web/grants/forms.html and https://www.grants.gov/web/grants/forms/r-r-family.html

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 field-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain SF-424 fields require special entries or handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable instructions: Field 3 - Date Received by State: Leave Blank. Field 4a - Federal Identifier: For ONR enter 'N00014'; for ARO enter 'W36QYT'; for AFOSR enter 'FA9550'. Field 4b - Agency Routing Number: ONR: enter the three-digit Research Topic Chief’s Code plus name in brackets (e.g., 331 [Smith, John]); where code has two digits add '0' after code. ARO: enter Research Topic Chief name. AFOSR: enter Topic Number and Research Topic Chief’s name (e.g., 12 [Smith, John]). Field 4c - If Changed/Corrected Application, enter previous Grants.gov tracking ID; otherwise leave blank. Field 5 & 14 - Email address entered will create EDA notification profile; DoD recommends a global business address. Field 7 - Type of Applicant: If Minority-Serving Institution, select 'Other' and note MI under 'Other (Specify)'. Field 9 - List the appropriate reviewing agency (ONR/AFOSR/ARO). Field 11 - Descriptive Title: Include 'MURI:' and ONR White Paper Tracking Number. Field 16 - Choose 'No' for Executive Order 12372. Field 17 - Certification: checking 'I Agree' certifies statements and legal obligations; AFOSR: if 'I Agree' is checked and SF-LLL is NOT uploaded, you are certifying you have no lobbying activities to disclose. Field 19 - Authorized Representative (AOR): the email populates EDA; if signature name doesn't match AOR, provide delegated signature authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project summary/abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract must identify the research problem and objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome if successful, and impact on DoD capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only characters available on a standard QWERTY keyboard; spell out Greek and other non-English letters/symbols. Graphics are not allowed. Length limit: one page or 4,000 characters including spaces, whichever is less. Do not include proprietary or confidential information. The abstract must be marked 'Approved for Public Release.' Abstracts of funded research will be posted on DTIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Related Other Project Information - human subjects & animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal must address human subject involvement and vertebrate animal use by completing Fields 1/1a and 2/2a of the R&R Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals involving human subjects, prior to award the Applicant must submit required documentation under 'Use of Human Subjects in Research' (Section F). For animal use, submit documents described under 'Use of Animals' (Section F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental compliance disclosure (Fields 4a-4d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address environmental compliance fields and indicate whether research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory and how compliance with environmental statutes/regulations will be ensured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal awardees must comply with environmental planning requirements (e.g., NEPA). Most DoD-funded basic/applied lab research is covered by NEPA categorical exclusion. Questions regarding NEPA or other environmental compliance should be referred to the technical point of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative / Field 8 attachment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach the entire proposal narrative to R&R Other Project Information form in Field 8 as a single PDF file labeled 'Technical Proposal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To attach, click 'Add attachment' and upload as a single PDF. Typing in the box is prohibited; save the file name as 'Technical Proposal.' The narrative should clearly describe the research, including objective and approach, and be written with the evaluation criteria in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical proposal required sections and cover page content
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical proposal must describe the research in specified sections and include a cover page (not included in page count) with specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page must include: ONR/ARO/AFOSR FOA number, title of proposal, technical contact (name, address, phone/fax, email), administrative/business contact (name, address, phone/fax, email), proposed period of performance (base and options), identity of prime Applicant and complete list of subawardees (if applicable). Include a Table of Contents (not included in page count) with section page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Approach content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Approach (included in page count) must describe objectives, scientific/technical concepts, complete research plan, data analysis approach, and what is innovative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss relationship to state-of-the-art and related efforts elsewhere, potential scientific breakthroughs, include appropriate literature citations/references. Given successful completion, describe expected results, new knowledge, or insights. The Technical Approach should include 'Future DoD Relevance' (description of potential DoD relevance/contributions) and 'Project Schedule and Milestones' (summary of schedule and milestones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Approach requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management Approach (included in page count) must describe team management, communication, data sharing, responsibility assignments, and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how and how often PI will communicate with co-investigators, how data will be made available within the team, how differences of opinion will be resolved, research and management responsibilities of team members, plans for research training of students, number of time-equivalent graduate students/undergraduates to be supported each year, and involvement of other students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator Qualifications section
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a discussion of the qualifications of the proposed Principal Investigator and any other key personnel (included in page count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant experience, leadership, and track record relevant to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (DMP) requirement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Management Plan (not included in page count) must describe which data, software, and other materials will be shared/preserved and how, or explain why sharing/preservation is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit: no more than 2 pages. Topics to address: types of data/software/materials to be produced; how data will be acquired; time/location of acquisition if pertinent; how data will be processed; file formats and naming conventions; quality assurance/quality control measures during collection/analysis/processing; description of dataset origin when using existing data; standards for data and metadata format and content; appropriate timeframe for preservation; justification balancing preservation value vs cost/administrative burden; statement that data cannot be made public when national security or CUI concerns exist (e.g., reference DoD Directive 5230.09). Also see DoD Instruction 3200.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload Bibliography/References Cited as a single PDF (Field 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure it is complete and attached as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities available for performing the proposed research and any additional facilities proposed to be acquired at Applicant expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate government-owned facilities to be used. Additional equipment will not be provided unless research cannot be completed by other practical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment justification and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any equipment available or proposed to be acquired and justify the need for each equipment item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate government-owned equipment that will be used. Provide vendor quotes for proposed capital equipment. Allowable items are normally limited to research equipment not already available; general-purpose equipment (PCs, laptops, office equipment) should not be requested unless used primarily or exclusively for the project and must include a statement of integration into the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget forms and general budget submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Grants.gov R&R Budget Form and provide detailed cost breakdowns by cost category and calendar periods; include option periods if proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use award start date 01 May 2024 for budget purposes. Budgets should include only costs to be expended during each calendar period. Include an option for two additional years. Attach a separate Adobe.pdf for Budget Justification under Section K of the R&R Budget form. All costs rounded to the nearest dollar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended funding profiles / total amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the agency-specific recommended funding profiles for FY25–FY30 and totals (three-year base subtotals and two-year option subtotals) as indicated for ONR, ARO, and AFOSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ONR three-year base subtotal $4,500,000 and five-year total $7,500,000. Available budget is subject to change based on funds availability. AFOSR will not consider requests above $15,000,000 including additional funding and cost-sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification required elements (itemized categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: The itemized budget justification must include detailed information for each cost element (Direct Labor, Administrative/Clerical, Fringe Benefits, Indirect Costs, Travel, Subawards/Subcontracts, Consultants, Materials & Supplies, Recipient Acquired Equipment, Other Direct Costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct Labor: individual labor categories/persons with hours and unburdened rates; provide escalation for outyears. Administrative/Clerical: normally indirect; direct charging only when major project requires extensive support and must be justified. Fringe Benefits: allowable if reasonable and required; attach institution's fringe benefits rate agreement. Indirect Costs: show rates and calculations for each category; provide memoranda if rates negotiated; if no negotiated rate, may elect de minimis 10% of modified total direct costs (see 2 CFR 200.414(f)). Travel: include purpose, origin/destination, approximate duration, number of travelers, estimated cost per trip, and justification based on historical average or reasonable basis; may include PI travel to peer reviews. Subawards/Subcontracts: provide description of subrecipient work and a detailed cost proposal from subrecipient using R&R budget form; include subrecipient name on top of budget justification. Consultants: breakdown of hours, hourly rate, other costs, signed consulting agreement or documentation, and consultant's statement of work if not included elsewhere. Materials & Supplies: itemized list with quantities, unit prices, and basis for estimate (quotes, prior purchases). Recipient Acquired Equipment: justify purchase, itemize costs and basis for estimate, and provide vendor quotes. Other Direct Costs: itemize items such as graduate assistant tuition, lab fees, publication costs with basis for estimates. Fee/Profit: unallowable under assistance agreements at prime or subaward level (may be permitted on contracts issued by the prime awardee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward/subcontract submission preferences and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide subrecipient cost proposals and supporting documentation before Government cost analysis and negotiations; DoD prefers subcontract information included with the prime proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcontractor's cost proposal may be provided in a sealed envelope with the prime proposal or via e-mail directly to the Program Officer at the same time the prime proposal is submitted; email should identify proposal title and prime Applicant and state the attachment is a subcontract.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) form collects degree type/year, biosketch/CV, and current & pending support information for all senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload biosketch/CV limited to 5 pages per CV. Current & Pending Support (no page limit) must include for each project: title and objectives; percentage per year devoted to other projects; total amount of support the individual is receiving or would receive if other proposals awarded; name and address of agencies/other parties; period of performance. Additional senior/key persons can be added. Applications missing required information may be returned without further review; DoD may request further details before final funding determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Related Personal Data (demographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application must include the Personal Data form with name fields for PI and Co-PIs; providing demographic information (gender, race, ethnicity, disability) is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If completing for multiple individuals, add each with 'Next Person.' Demographic info may be accessible to reviewers but will not be considered in evaluation. Applicants may choose 'Do not wish to provide.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) & SAM maintenance during award
rubrics_metrics.description: All Applicants must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid UEI in each application, and maintain active SAM registration with current information while having an active Federal award or application under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Applicant has not complied by the time the agency is ready to make an award, the agency may deem the Applicant not qualified and make an award to another Applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding restrictions – Section 889 (telecommunications and surveillance equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 889 (NDAA FY2019) prohibits obligating or expending grant funds to procure/obtain/extend/renew contracts for equipment, services, or systems that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component or critical technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered telecommunications equipment examples: equipment produced by Huawei or ZTE; video surveillance/telecom equipment by Hytera, Hikvision, or Dahua; telecommunications or video surveillance services provided by such entities; equipment/services produced/provided by entities believed to be owned/controlled by a covered foreign country (People’s Republic of China). In implementing the prohibition, agency heads shall prioritize available funding and technical support to help affected entities transition from covered equipment. See Public Law 115-232 section 889 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and account setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants submitting via Grants.gov must register their organization in SAM and create a Grants.gov account and organizational profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM registrations may take 7–10 days, so register early. Steps: 1) Register with SAM. 2) Create a Grants.gov account. 3) Add a profile to the Grants.gov account and enter the UEI when adding an organizational profile. 4) EBiz POC authorizes profile roles (including AOR). 5) Track role status. Electronic Signature: the name of the organization's AOR that submitted the application is inserted into the signature line of the application, serving as the electronic signature. Ensure the EBiz POC authorizes individuals who can make legally binding commitments as AOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper submission channels and distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must be submitted via the channel specified (e.g., FedConnect for ONR) and NOT via Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the correct submission portal for white papers and full proposals to avoid rejection or misrouting.
